context.note: CODE-DESIGNER read REQ-184 in full from docs/requirements.yaml plus the real, already-merged REQ-183/REQ-182/REQ-181/REQ-069 code before drafting. Key findings: (1) no existing context function lists webhook_delivery_attempts rows -- a NEW function, Letflow.Webhooks.list_delivery_attempts/3, is required (design section 1); it reuses the module's existing private get/2 helper for the tenant-scoped existence check, so cross-tenant-404 is automatic, not reimplemented. (2) endpoint_policy_key("GET", "/webhooks/subscriptions/:id/deliveries") and required_permission(:WebhookSubscriptionsManage) => :WebhooksManage ALREADY EXIST in lib/letflow/api/authorization.ex (lines ~293-294, ~425) -- zero authorization.ex changes are in scope for REQ-184; this is called out explicitly in design section 3 so ELIXIR-DEV does not add a duplicate clause. (3) The route is added as a fifth authz_get clause on the EXISTING Letflow.Routers.Webhooks module (REQ-182), not a new router file. (4) limit param: default 20 (matching the one real SPA caller's literal usage), enforced via a database-level LIMIT, ordered attempted_at desc then attempt_count desc for determinism (design section 4, flagged as this design's own choice in the open-questions section since no AC states an ordering). (5) Response allowlist mirrors subscription_json/1's existing hand-built-map idiom (INV-2) -- 9 exact fields per the SPA's WebhookDeliveryAttempt type, independently re-read from web/src/types/api.ts and web/src/api/dlq.ts's parseDeliveryAttempt/1 (which throws on any field-shape mismatch). (6) AC6's moduledoc disclosure is already present in the router module from REQ-182 and just needs extending, not authoring fresh -- design section 5.3 gives ELIXIR-DEV the exact extension points. No implementation code (no .ex/.ts fenced bodies) appears in the artefact -- verified by grep for defmodule/defp/case/with-with-do blocks and triple-backtick fences before this handoff was written; this branch's design doc previously went through two CODE-DESIGN-VALIDATOR FAIL/rework cycles for a DIFFERENT requirement (REQ-157) on literal-code grounds per docs/anti-patterns.md-adjacent history, so this artefact was drafted with that failure mode specifically in mind.

acceptance_criteria: GET /api/v1/webhooks/subscriptions/:id/deliveries returns {items: [...]} with each item's fields matching WebhookDeliveryAttempt exactly (delivery_id, subscription_id, event_type, status, http_status_code, attempted_at, attempt_count, max_attempts, last_error)
the route honors the limit param, demonstrated by a test with more delivery attempts than the requested limit returning exactly limit items
the route requires the WebhooksManage permission from REQ-069's matrix -- a caller lacking it receives 403
a caller from a different tenant naming a real subscription id belonging to tenant A receives 404, never 403, regardless of whether that subscription has delivery attempts
a request against a non-existent subscription id returns 404

the route module's moduledoc states explicitly that R-Co's webhooks.zig was not inspected in this batch (unreachable from the drafting environment) and that the SPA's already-committed contract was the binding source of truth instead
